1. ServiceProvider is `IDisposable`. You should be disposing it when you are done. I don't see you disposing it above.
2. The reference you show above with DependencyInjectionEventSource is a WeakReference. Which means if there are no other references to the object, the GC is free to clean the object up.

1. i can't get ServiceProvider reference, because HubConnectionBuilder.Build() not return. (HubConnectionBuilder is SignalR client code https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnectionBuilder.cs)
2. gc can free WeakReference 's object,but it can't free List WeakReference  item ` List<WeakReference<ServiceProvider>> _providers = new();`

> i can't get ServiceProvider reference, because HubConnectionBuilder.Build() not return. (HubConnectionBuilder is SignalR client code

@davidfowl @BrennanConroy - thoughts on Disposing the `ServiceProvider` in HubConnectionBuilder?
The builder doesn't dispose the service provider, when you dispose the HubConnection itself the service provider gets disposed.

> The builder doesn't dispose the service provider, when you dispose the HubConnection itself the service provider gets disposed. I call the HubConnection.DisposeAsync ,but serviceprovider not disposed

You can see the code that disposes the connection here https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/7cb457bdaac8de9214391a9b9b273821d01c2300/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnection.cs#L558-L570

> You can see the code that disposes the connection here https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/7cb457bdaac8de9214391a9b9b273821d01c2300/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnection.cs#L558-L570 HubConnection dispose the child service provider ,but root service provider is not dispose DependencyInjectionEventSource reference the root service provider

I think it does dispose the services, but it doesn't dispose the `ServiceProvider` instance itself. This wasn't a problem before .NET 6 because we didn't do anything besides disposing the root scope itself, now we clean up the event source as well so there's a leak.
I think disposing the root IServiceProvider and ServiceProvider should be identical. Whether we change signalR as well is separate.
cc @BrennanConroy as an FYI
@davidfowl do you think this is critical to fix for .NET 7.0? or can it wait to 8.0? from reading looks we have this behavior in 6.0 too.
I think we should fix this in .NET 7 and 6

Got it, this meets the bar for 7.0 if we'd service it in 6.0.  @eerhardt do we have enough info from @davidfowl's [suggestion](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/73832#issuecomment-1213313164) to try out a fix?  How risky would it be?

> do we have enough info from @davidfowl's https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/73832#issuecomment-1213313164 to try out a fix?

Yes, I believe so.

> How risky would it be?

Fairly low risk. If someone was Disposing the "root" ServiceProviderEngineScope, but not the `ServiceProvider`, and was still trying to use the `ServiceProvider` in their application, they could still get Singleton services from it. So disposing the `ServiceProvider` along with the "root" ServiceProviderEngineScope may break something that currently works today, but isn't supposed to work.
Where do we track the backport?

> Where do we track the backport?

I'll start the backport now. will tag you on that. The backport will be for .NET 7.0 and .NET 6.0 too.

review_comments: It may help to add a comment here explaining the situation and the reasoning.

Are we OK with the extra loop a Dispose will cause now?

Before:
`ServiceProvider.Dispose()` => `ServiceProviderEngineScope.Dispose()`

Now:
`ServiceProvider.Dispose()` => `ServiceProviderEngineScope.Dispose()` => `ServiceProvider.Dispose()` => `ServiceProviderEngineScope.Dispose()` (which finally breaks out of the cycle.

We could fix this (if necessary) by checking `if (IsRootScope && !RootProvider._disposed)`.

I thought about it before and didn't like to change _disposed to be not private. I don't have a strong feeling though. If you think it is worth it, I can apply it. (may be introduce internal IsDisposed method in the service provider)
Thinking more, I think it is ok to introduce IsDisposed. I'll do that.
Why cant this just noop internally?

It is simpler. no? 

More code, more bugs :-) imagine in the future we add anything to the ServicePrivder dispose method.
